Every critique item was checked against the code. All evidence lines were confirmed. Verdicts:
- C1 Relay transfer lane (sage_handoff_service.py:413-439): ACCEPTED. New increment adt-6c. Release gate: ORB_ADT is not switched on at any site where Sage runs until adt-6c lands; the census (adt-13a) depends on it.

- C3 a vacated bed could read available: ACCEPTED. needs_cleaning is also derived from the ledger, so no sync is needed. adt-5 depends on the board rule (adt-4a), not on adt-7.
- C4 ledger ordering: ACCEPTED. The ledger migration is now adt-2 and comes before the admission columns (adt-3), which write 'location_linked' rows.
- C5 second bed writer: ACCEPTED. With ORB_ADT on, the housekeeping register route refuses bed units; register_unit_on takes a ward_id that skips _canonical_ward.
- C6 renames: ACCEPTED. A ward code or bed label is immutable once referenced; retire and recreate.
- C7 permissions pre-deciding rulings: ACCEPTED. ADT_WRITE is split into ADT_BED and ADT_TRANSFER; nurses get nothing until ADT-S7; absconded closure lives only under S3; the clerk gets no department change until ADT-S8.
- C8 swaps toggling and one-sided scope: ACCEPTED. Both sides in scope, Idempotency-Key required, expected bed ids checked.
- C9 text-only lanes: ACCEPTED, with a different schema mechanism. AdmissionRequest keeps ward: str and bed: str (an empty string already passes today) and gains optional awaiting_bed, ward_id and bed_id, so the flag-off 422 contract does not change at all. Text resolution, awaiting and unlinked are section 5.
- C10 no ledger start: ACCEPTED. wards.ledger_complete_from; earlier windows report 'insufficient data'; ends before the flag fall back to summaries. Census resized (adt-13a plus adt-13b, 5.5 days).

- C12 Ward Record re-cost: ACCEPTED. About 54.5 engineer-days plus OPD create-or-find, and it cannot ship clerk admission or 'left the ward' until S3 and S5 are ruled (section 12).

What the board, NEWS2 and Sage show as 'latest' after a readmission is a clinical display decision, so it is raised as new safety ruling ADT-S9 rather than decided here; the readmit entry point stays closed until adt-18b.
- C14 a wrong death cannot be undone: ACCEPTED. Server-side read-back (confirm_mrn) in adt-8a; reopen in adt-8b, limited to ends with no discharge summary. While fixing it I found my design also pre-decided P8 (portal login deactivation on death); that step now waits for P8.
- C15 boarder placement before S6: ACCEPTED IN PART. Placement needs an explicit acknowledgement naming who will and will not see the chart, is audited as clinical_access, and posts a system line to the case room. REJECTED: refusing boarders under strict mode. When the home ward is full that refuses an admission, which is a care-delivery decision that belongs to S6.

- C17 cover check deadlock: ACCEPTED. Department cover and ward lookups are resolved before BEGIN IMMEDIATE, as transfer_patient already does.
- C18 dual audit and dual tasks: ACCEPTED. The frontdesk route skips its post-commit audit when it delegates; one task key per discharge.
- C19 disposition double count: ACCEPTED. Match by admission_id, then by stay window; conflicts are flagged, never inserted twice.
- C20 two admission start sources: ACCEPTED. stay_start helper adopted by census, billing and forecast.
- C21 migration hazards: ACCEPTED all four (lazy-path ALTER guard, explicit rowid copy, restated flag-off guarantee, vocabulary trigger instead of CHECK on the ledger).
- C22 adt-0 breaks shell tests: ACCEPTED. adt-0 adds TABS, i18n and admin tab entries and amends the default-ON tests.
- C23 ward_clerk with the flag off: ACCEPTED. Creation refused unless ORB_ADT is on; honest off state in the shell.
- C24 assorted: ACCEPTED all five. On the portal mirror: no reader of a patient login's users.department was found except the Relay lane's department list, which is exactly how a ward label could be written as a department; adt-6c replaces that list with covering departments. locate_admission_on leaves the portal mirror as written at admission, on purpose.
- C25 sizing and scope: ACCEPTED. adt-3, adt-6 and adt-13 are split; the facilities table, the per-bed counts_in_census override, gender_policy and sort_key are dropped. ward_rooms stays (isolation rooms drive terminal cleans).

1. PRINCIPLES
- One source per fact. Occupancy is derived from the admission (admissions.bed_id on an active admission). Cleaning state stays with housekeeping, read together with the ledger. patient_movements is the history. The text mirrors (patients.ward/bed, admissions.ward/bed) are still written because about 34 server files read them, by ONE writer, adt_service.locate_admission_on.
- No new value in patients.status or admissions.status (22 readers filter on them; widening means rebuilding patients). Presence lives in admissions.presence_status. Every end of stay is status 'discharged' plus admissions.discharge_type, except roster close, which keeps the file's 'transferred' and sets discharge_type 'transferred_out'.
- Flag off means no behaviour change. Schema changes always apply, because migrations run on every database; new columns stay NULL; SELECT * readers may carry new NULL keys in JSON; every /api/adt route returns 404. Snapshot tests pin the rows written by admit, transfer and discharge with the flag off.
- Additive migrations: ADD COLUMN, new tables with no foreign keys, partial and expression indexes, one statement per execute, IF NOT EXISTS plus PRAGMA table_info guards. The only rebuild is patient_movements (no FK children). patients and admissions are never rebuilt; users only through _rebuild_users_role_check.
- Every ADT write: resolves departments, cover and master rows first; then runs in db_session(immediate=True) as the outermost session; checks the expected current state; writes its audit inside the same transaction (log_audit_event(db=...)), so an unwritable audit rolls the move back; catches db_backend.DBIntegrityError; stamps times with services.clinical_time.utc_iso_now()/to_utc_iso(); passes target_id as a string; carries an Idempotency-Key.
- A medico-legal row is never deleted. Corrections are new rows; voids are stamped.

2. FEATURE FLAGS (server/config.py)
- _opt_in_enabled(env): OFF unless 1/true/on/yes. OPT_IN_MODULES = {'adt': 'ORB_ADT'}, merged into enabled_modules() and HOSPITAL_MODULE_ENV so /api/health publishes it. test_money's pin becomes: every non-opt-in module defaults on and every opt-in module defaults off.
- ORB_ADT (off): master, board, census and ADT routes, plus master-aware admit, transfer and discharge.
- ORB_ADT_STRICT_LOCATIONS (off, needs ORB_ADT): refuse an unlisted ward or bed on every lane (F104).
- ORB_ADT_BACKTIME_HOURS (72), ORB_ADT_RESERVATION_MINUTES (120), ORB_ADT_ABSCONDED_CLOSE_HOURS (24, advisory prompt only).
- require_adt_module returns 404 when off. Frontend: OPT_IN_MODULE_IDS = ['adt'], DEFAULT_MODULE_FLAGS adt: false, and a failed or non-OK health probe keeps adt false, so an opt-in module fails toward hidden.
- Release gate (documented in config next to ORB_ADT): do not switch ORB_ADT on at a site with Sage enabled before adt-6c, nor rely on census or NABH figures before adt-8a, adt-8c and adt-6c.

3. DATA MODEL (8 migrations, provisional 48 to 55)
M-a (adt-1), bed master:
- wards(id PK 'WRD-...', facility_code NOT NULL DEFAULT 'MAIN' (a plain label until the multi-site epic adds a table), code NOT NULL, name, department NOT NULL, ward_type CHECK(general, icu, hdu, nicu, picu, maternity, daycare, emergency, isolation, other), default_bed_class, cleaning_tracked INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, register_complete INT DEFAULT 0, register_complete_at, register_complete_by, ledger_complete_from, is_active, created_by, created_at, updated_at). UNIQUE INDEX (facility_code, LOWER(TRIM(code))). code is the label written to admissions.ward and is immutable once referenced; name is free.
- ward_rooms(id PK, ward_id NOT NULL, code, name, room_type CHECK(bay, private, semi_private, isolation, icu_cubicle, other), is_isolation INT, is_active, created_at, updated_at); UNIQUE (ward_id, LOWER(TRIM(code))).
- bed_classes(code PK, name, bed_day_service_code, is_critical_care INT, counts_in_census INT DEFAULT 1, is_active, created_at, updated_at). No seed.
- housekeeping_units ADD COLUMN ward_id, room_id, bed_class, is_temporary INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, retired_at; INDEX (ward_id, is_active). The same columns go into the shared HOUSEKEEPING_TABLES CREATE (fresh databases) and ensure_housekeeping_schema runs a PRAGMA-guarded ALTER for each, so the lazy path can never recreate the old shape. A unit with unit_type 'bed' and a ward_id IS the physical bed; unit_code = '<ward code>/<bed label>' because idx_hk_units_code is global. Bed label is immutable once referenced.
- bed_master_events(id, entity_type CHECK(ward, room, bed, bed_class), entity_id, action, detail_json, reason, actor_user_id, occurred_at), append-only by no-update and no-delete triggers; no patient data.
M-c (adt-2), the ledger: patient_movements in a numbered migration with three cases: absent (create), old shape (rebuild in the runner's transaction, copying rowid explicitly, recreating the 3 indexes), new shape (no-op). New shape drops the movement_type CHECK for a BEFORE INSERT vocabulary trigger (RAISE ABORT), so widening later is DROP/CREATE TRIGGER. Vocabulary: admission, bed_assigned, transfer, bed_change, bed_swap, leave_start, leave_end, absconded, absconded_return, discharge, location_linked, correction. New columns: from_ward_id, from_bed_id, to_ward_id, to_bed_id, end_type, discharge_summary_id, corrects_movement_id, recorded_at, detail_json. moved_at is when it happened (back-timeable); recorded_at is the server clock. New indexes (to_bed_id, moved_at), (from_bed_id, moved_at), (movement_type, moved_at). frontdesk_service imports the DDL from migrations.
M-b (adt-3), where the admission is: admissions ADD COLUMN ward_id, bed_id, bed_shared_reason, admitted_at, presence_status (NULL means on the ward; on_leave, absconded), presence_since, discharge_type (routine, referred_out, transferred_out, dama, lama, absconded, death), discharged_by. Vocabularies by BEFORE INSERT and BEFORE UPDATE OF presence_status, discharge_type triggers; a note beside _atomic_table_rebuild says a future admissions rebuild must carry them. Bed lock: UNIQUE INDEX idx_admissions_active_bed ON admissions(bed_id) WHERE status='active' AND bed_id IS NOT NULL AND bed_shared_reason IS NULL (safe to build: every bed_id is NULL). INDEX (ward_id, status).
M-h (adt-8a): nabh_discharge_dispositions ADD COLUMN source DEFAULT 'admin' ('admin' or 'adt'), voided_at, voided_by, void_reason, needs_reconciliation INT DEFAULT 0; INDEX (admission_id). NABH readers filter voided_at IS NULL.
M-d (adt-7): housekeeping_movement_links(movement_id PK, unit_id, effect CHECK(occupied, occupied_unclean, vacated, task_raised, skipped), task_id, applied_at).
M-e (adt-12): bed_reservations(id, bed_id, ward_id, patient_id, admission_id, purpose CHECK(admission, transfer, post_op, elective, other), note, status CHECK(active, fulfilled, released, expired), reserved_by, reserved_at, expires_at, closed_at, closed_by, close_reason), UNIQUE (bed_id) WHERE status='active'.
M-f (adt-17): 'ward_clerk' through _rebuild_users_role_check, one migration shared with the OPD epic's receptionist.
M-g (adt-18a): partial UNIQUE admissions(patient_id) WHERE status='active', built only after a duplicate report is empty.
Census has no table in v1.

4. BED STATUS ON THE BOARD (derived, in this precedence)
1. retired (only possible for an unoccupied, unreserved bed).
2. occupied, occupied_on_leave, occupied_absconded: an active admission holds bed_id. If housekeeping says out_of_service the tile reads 'Occupied, bed reported out of service' and still shows the occupant.
3. reserved (with the same out-of-service marker when it applies).
4. out_of_service.
5. needs_cleaning when ANY of: housekeeping says vacant_dirty; housekeeping says occupied and nobody occupies the bed; the bed's latest vacating movement (from_bed_id = bed, moved_at) is newer than the bed's latest housekeeping event into vacant_ready. The third rule needs no sync, so a bed vacated before adt-7, or between two sync runs, never reads available.
6. cleaning (cleaning_in_progress).
7. available (vacant_ready and no newer vacating movement).
Cleaning not tracked: when ORB_HOUSEKEEPING is off or the ward's cleaning_tracked is 0, rules 5 to 7 collapse to 'Vacant, cleaning not tracked' and no clean-related warning is raised (otherwise a site without housekeeping would see every bed as needing cleaning and the S2 warning would fire on every admission).
Each tile carries minutes in state, isolation and temporary markers and the bed class; for an occupant inside the caller's scope also name, MRN, treating department and 'Boarder from <dept>' when it differs from the ward's.

5. TEXT RESOLUTION, AWAITING AND UNLINKED (locate_admission_on)
- Ids given: used as given, validated against the master.
- Text only (Scribe quick admit, roster import, old clients): an exact case- and space-insensitive match of the ward to wards.code links ward_id; an exact match of the bed label within that ward links bed_id. The mirrors are then written in the master's spelling. No match keeps the typed text and leaves the id NULL (strict off) or refuses with words (strict on, adt-16).
- Awaiting bed = active admission with no bed text and no bed_id. Unlinked bed = bed text present and bed_id NULL. They are separate lists; the unlinked list offers 'Link to master bed' (bed.master, writes 'location_linked').
- POST /admissions/{id}/bed refuses when bed text is present unless the body says correction: true, which writes a 'correction' row. A clerk can therefore never overwrite where a patient actually lies by assigning a second bed.
- Retired beds are refused. An out_of_service bed needs a typed reason, recorded in detail_json (housekeeping's rule: refuse a record, never a patient).

6. SERVICES
bed_master_service.py (new): list_master; save_ward (department must be a covering department or declared in site.toml, resolved before the session; a ward with no clinical cover is saved and marked 'admissions refused until a doctor or nurse covers <dept>'); save_room; register_beds (bulk labels or a range, one immediate session through housekeeping_service.register_unit_on, with the bed_master_events rows and the audit in the same transaction; default state vacant_dirty); update_bed and rename guards (code and label immutable once any admission or movement references them); retire_bed (refused while occupied or reserved); save_bed_class; import_site_config_wards (idempotent); reconciliation_report (matched, unlinked, doubled); link_admissions (confirmed by the bed manager; never links a doubled bed); mark_register_complete (refused while the ward has unlinked active admissions or doubled beds; stamps register_complete_at and ledger_complete_from); bed_board; available_beds; resolve_bed_reference (exact lookup for later R026 work; not wired into Sage).
housekeeping_service: register_unit_on(db, ..., ward_id, room_id, bed_class, is_temporary); register_unit stays a wrapper. With ward_id, ward text is wards.code and _canonical_ward is skipped.
adt_service.py (new, the single ADT writer):
- current_location(patient_id): the one reader for LIS, pharmacy and diet.
- record_movement_on(db, ...): the single ledger writer.
- locate_admission_on(db, ...): the single writer of ward_id, bed_id and both text mirrors. Checks the lock, expected_bed_id, reservations, retired and out-of-service rules, and the boarder acknowledgement: when the ward's department differs from the treating department it requires boarder_acknowledged, else 409 with the words 'Nurses on <ward> (<host dept>) will not be able to open this chart. The <treating dept> team keeps it.' An acknowledged placement writes a clinical_access audit 'boarder_placed' and a system line in the patient's case room (messages, is_bot 1, sender 'system') in the same transaction. Scope is unchanged (S6).
- assign_bed; transfer (rules A, B and C verbatim; cover resolved before the session; keep_location option for the Relay lane); change_bed; swap_beds (both admissions in the caller's scope, both expected bed ids, NULL step so the index never trips); correct_movement.

Disposition: an existing row with this admission_id is updated (if its type differs, needs_reconciliation=1 and the admin value is kept); else an admission-less row for the patient inside [stay_start, end + 24 h] is linked (same conflict rule); else a new row with source 'adt'. death_within_48h derived from stay_start. Restores status, re-locates the same bed if free else awaiting bed, writes a 'correction' row pointing at the discharge row, voids the disposition (stamped, not deleted), restores the portal login only if the end deactivated it (detail_json), lists bundles F050 cancelled without restoring them, audits clinical_access 'stay_reopened'. adt_census_service.py (adt-13a): hospital-local days (services.hospital_time); midnight census; admissions, transfers in and out, ends by type (status 'transferred' maps to transferred_out); deaths; per-stay inpatient days; licensed and available beds (census beds minus out-of-service time from housekeeping_unit_events; temporary beds excluded); occupancy; ALOS; return to ICU within 48 h. Changes to existing services: admission_service (master-aware admit and choices when on); frontdesk_service.transfer_patient (delegates when on); discharge_service (uses _close_admission_on; optional discharge_type); housekeeping_service (register_unit_on, sync_adt_movements, sweep keyed on the ended admission's bed); sage_handoff_service._dispatch_to_transfer (delegates when on, adt-6c); nabh_service (auto dispositions, void filter, per-stay days, QI-UTL-01 and QI-OUT-04 for complete wards); billing_service (type filter, class-by-day pricing, stay_start); forecast_service (stay helpers, master capacity, refresh after master writes); roster_import (update and close through adt_service when on); impact_service and bridge_routes (stay_end).

7. ROUTES (server/routes/adt_routes.py, prefix /api/adt, all behind require_adt_module)
- Every write takes an Idempotency-Key header (stored on the movement; a replay returns the first result) and, for moves, expected_bed_id (or both for a swap); a mismatch is 409 'state_changed'.
- Bed setup (bed.master): GET /master (adt.read); POST/PATCH /master/wards, /master/rooms, /master/beds, /master/bed-classes; POST /master/beds/{id}/retire; POST /master/wards/{id}/register-complete; POST /master/import-site-config; GET /master/reconciliation; POST /master/reconciliation/link.
- Board: GET /board?ward_id= (adt.read; identity only for in-scope occupants; phi_access read audit); GET /awaiting-bed (two lists: awaiting, unlinked); GET /beds/available?ward_id=.
- Moves: POST /admissions/{id}/bed and /bed-change (adt.bed or patient.write); POST /transfers (adt.transfer or patient.write); POST /bed-swaps (adt.bed or patient.write; both admissions in scope); POST /movements/{id}/correct (adt.bed or patient.write). Scope failures return 404, not 403.
- Presence: POST /admissions/{id}/leave, /leave-end, /absconded, /returned (adt.presence or patient.write).
- End of stay: POST /admissions/{id}/end with confirm_mrn (death, lama, dama: discharge.generate plus scope, today's authority); POST /admissions/{id}/reopen (discharge.generate plus scope via the ended admission's department, reason, confirm_mrn). Absconded closure and the clerk's departure open only after S3.
- History and reservations: GET /patients/{patient_id}/movements (adt.read, scope, read audit); POST /reservations; POST /reservations/{id}/release.
- Census: GET /census?from&to&ward_id, /census.csv.
Changes to existing routes: POST /api/admissions/admit gains optional ward_id, bed_id, awaiting_bed, admitted_at, bed_shared_reason, out_of_service_reason, boarder_acknowledged (honoured only when on; ward and bed keep their str types). GET /api/admissions/options returns master beds with derived status when on. POST /api/vigil/patients/{id}/discharge takes optional discharge_type (routine, referred_out, transferred_out, dama) and points lama, absconded and death to End of stay. POST /api/vigil/patients (legacy) returns 404 with words when on. POST /api/frontdesk/transfers delegates and skips its own post-commit audit. POST /api/housekeeping/units refuses unit_type 'bed' (create or edit) when on, 409 'managed_in_beds_setup'. Admin user creation refuses role ward_clerk when ORB_ADT is off.

8. PERMISSIONS (server/permissions.py, mirrored in src/lib/roles.ts; roles.py stays the role authority)
| Permission | Allows | Held by |
|---|---|---|
| ADT_READ 'adt.read' | Board, availability, census, movement history; identity of in-scope occupants, read-audited | admin, doctor; ward_clerk (adt-17); nurse only after ADT-S7 |
| ADT_BED 'adt.bed' | Assign, change bed, swap, correct, reserve; never changes the treating department | admin, ward_clerk (adt-17); doctors through the patient.write arm |
| ADT_TRANSFER 'adt.transfer' | Change the treating department (a scope change) | admin; doctors through the patient.write arm; ward_clerk only after ADT-S8 |
| ADT_PRESENCE 'adt.presence' | Leave, absconded, returned | admin; doctors through the patient.write arm; nurse and ward_clerk only after ADT-S7 |
| BED_MASTER 'bed.master' | Bed setup, reconciliation link, register complete | admin |
End of stay keeps discharge.generate plus scope; no ADT permission ends a stay. Nurses gain nothing in this epic until ADT-S7.

9. AUDIT
- New fail-closed category 'patient_movement' (audit_service._FAIL_CLOSED_CATEGORIES), emitter in adt-3. Cross-department transfers, boarder placements, ends of stay and reopens are clinical_access. All written inside the transaction.
- Action types: patient_admitted_to_bed, bed_assigned, patient_transferred, bed_changed, beds_swapped, movement_corrected, admission_location_linked, boarder_placed; leave_started, leave_ended, patient_absconded, absconded_patient_returned; stay_ended (end_type in metadata), death_recorded, stay_reopened, disposition_reconcile_flagged; bed_reserved, bed_reservation_released; bed_board_viewed and patient_movements_viewed (phi_access with patient_ids). Master edits: category 'facilities' plus a bed_master_events row.

10. UI AND SHELL
- adt-0: 'adt' joins HospitalModuleId, HOSPITAL_MODULE_IDS, HOSPITAL_MODULE_PANEL_PATH ('./pages/panels/BedBoardPanel.tsx'), the glob list, TABS (label 'Beds', pillar 'Beds and Admissions'), HOSPITAL_MODULE_TABS (admin) and en.json/hi.json nav and subtitle. The panel file arrives in adt-4a, so until then the tab is 'not installed' and absent.
- ROLE_CONFIG.ward_clerk = {home 'adt', tabs [adt], primaryAction null}; with the flag off the clerk sees 'Beds is switched off on this site. Ask your administrator.' instead of an empty Vigil.
- BedBoardPanel: Board (ward picker limited to scope, tiles by room, counts strip, tile actions), Awaiting bed and Unlinked, Census (adt-13a), Setup (adt-4b, bed.master).
- src/components/adt/: BedPicker (status words; out-of-service reason box; boarder acknowledgement text from the server), MoveDrawer, PresenceDrawer, EndStayDrawer (typed MRN read-back, time within the back-time window, open escalations and bundles listed as F050 does, reason for LAMA and DAMA), ReopenStayDialog.
- Edits: AdmitPatientModal (BedPicker and 'No bed yet' when flags.adt), FrontDeskPanel transfer modal, VigilPanel discharge type select, Vigil board and NursePanel 'Not on ward since HH:MM' chip, HousekeepingPanel 'Beds and rooms' links to Beds setup when on, UsersPanel hides ward_clerk when off.
- Wrappers in a new src/api/adt.ts, not client.ts. Quiet Clinical tokens, status text vs fill tokens, check-contrast gate. No em dashes. The patient portal does not change.

11. CUTOVER AND READERS
- A ward's ADT figures start at wards.ledger_complete_from (set by register-complete, which requires every active admission on the ward to be linked). Earlier days are 'insufficient data', never zero. Ends before the flag come from discharge_summaries through stay_end.
- adt-8c teaches every summary-keyed reader about ends without a summary: forecast, impact, NABH readmission (death excluded by type), bridge discharge view, housekeeping sweep (keyed on the ended admission, not the patient's current labels), /discharged list time. The m15 and billing _discharge_stamp comments are updated, because admissions.discharged_at becomes a stay-end source for ADT stays (status remains THE discharge test).

12. CONNECTIONS TO OTHER EPICS
- OPD registration: create-or-find feeds adt-18a; 'admit from OPD' creates an awaiting-bed admission; one users rebuild for receptionist and ward_clerk; the one-active-admission index owned jointly.
- Single medication-order store: reads current_location and movements for transfer reconciliation (W105), in-transit dispenses (ward receipt is department-scoped) and orders at death (P8). This epic does not touch helix_service.
- LIS (collection lists, labels), pharmacy indents, diet: read current_location.
- Multi-site: wards.facility_code is the hook; that epic adds the facilities table and facility scoping.
- Billing: bed classes carry the bed-day code (adt-15). NABH: dispositions, occupancy, return to ICU, per-stay days. Housekeeping: turnaround, bed-id matching, single register writer.
- Ward Record profile (P2), re-costed: adt-0, 1, 2, 3, 4a, 5, 6a, 6b, 8a, 8b, 8c, 9, 10, 16, 17, 17b, 18a, 18b = about 54.5 engineer-days, plus OPD create-or-find, against the 11 to 17.5 days the sales plan assumed (SALES_PLAN_2026-10.md:184). adt-4b is left out (the founder loads one ward through the import API), adt-6c (Sage is off in the profile) and adt-7 (housekeeping off). It cannot ship clerk admission or 'left the ward' until S5 and S3 are ruled (adt-17b), and the returning-patient path waits for ADT-S9 (adt-18b).
- A future inbound HL7 ADT feed would call adt_service.

TOTAL
About 78.5 engineer-days (about 16 weeks) for the whole epic. The core (adt-0 to adt-8c) is about 41.5 days.

product_rulings.question: ADT-S1. When the chosen bed already holds an admitted patient, what happens? Today it is warned and logged, never blocked (admission_service.py:120). The bed label is how nurses, the eMAR round and Sage find a patient.
product_rulings.options: (a) Block, and offer 'add an extra bed' that creates a temporary bed with its own label (GM-1/12A). (b) Allow a deliberate shared bed with a typed reason, recorded; accidental double booking refused by the database either way. (c) Keep today's warning only.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). Every patient keeps a unique bed label and an extra bed is counted honestly. Until ruled, the build ships (b), which never blocks a patient.

product_rulings.question: ADT-S2. May a patient be admitted or moved into a bed housekeeping has not recorded clean, including one awaiting a terminal clean after an isolation patient? And into a bed recorded out of service?
product_rulings.options: (a) Allow with a reason, recorded. (b) Warn only. (c) Block beds awaiting a terminal clean unless a named person authorises it; allow standard-clean beds and out-of-service beds with a reason.
product_rulings.recommendation: (c). Until ruled, the build warns and records, and needs a typed reason for an out-of-service bed. Wards that do not track cleaning raise no clean warning.

product_rulings.question: ADT-S3. Who may end an admission, by type: routine departure after a doctor's discharge, LAMA, DAMA, absconded closure, death? May the Ward Record clerk mark 'left the ward' with no discharge summary?
product_rulings.options: Per type: doctor only; doctor or nurse; clerk or bed manager; time windows for absconded closure.
product_rulings.recommendation: Death, LAMA and DAMA stay doctor-only (discharge.generate, scope, read-back). A nurse or clerk records the physical departure only after a doctor's discharge exists. The bed manager closes an absconded stay after 24 h (site setting), with police intimation noted for MLC cases. In the Ward Record profile the clerk may record 'left the ward' with the time.

product_rulings.question: ADT-S4. While a patient is on leave or absconded, do they stay on clinical boards, and do obs-due timers, medication-due lists, escalation ladders, sepsis auto-start and the vitals simulator keep running?
product_rulings.options: (a) Stay on boards with a 'Not on ward' chip; obs and med due paused with the reason; escalation paused, not closed; resumes on return. (b) Remove from boards until return. (c) No change.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). Absconded patients with an open escalation also notify the treating doctor in Relay. Removing them recreates the orphaning failure.

product_rulings.question: ADT-S5. May a non-clinical ward clerk create an admission, and what does the chart show for allergies and other clinical fields until a clinician completes them? Orb cannot tell NKDA from 'never asked' today (allergy_interlock.py:364).
product_rulings.options: (a) Yes: clinical fields read 'Not yet assessed', never NKDA; the interlock treats it as unknown; the board flags 'admission assessment due'. (b) Only doctors admit.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). Required for the Ward Record and front-office admission. 'Not yet assessed' must never print as NKDA.

product_rulings.question: ADT-S6. A boarder lies on another department's ward. Scope follows the treating department, so the host ward's nurses cannot open the chart of a patient in their own beds. Whose board are they on?
product_rulings.options: (a) Both: host-ward nurses get shift-board and nursing access, the treating team keeps medical ownership. (b) Treating department only (today). (c) The ward's department only.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a), built as one change to PATIENT_DEPARTMENT_SQL and its sage_service twin under the parity test. Until ruled, a boarder placement needs an explicit acknowledgement naming who will and will not see the chart, is audited as clinical_access and posts a case-room line; scope is unchanged.

product_rulings.question: ADT-S7. Who may record leave and absconded (which, once S4 is built, pauses clinical timers), and do nurses get the Beds tab read-only for their ward?
product_rulings.options: Doctors only; doctors and nurses; doctors, nurses and the ward clerk. Nurses get the read-only board or not.
product_rulings.recommendation: Doctors and nurses record leave and absconded; the clerk records them only in the Ward Record profile, where no timer runs. Nurses get the read-only board scoped to their ward, no master edits and no transfers. Until ruled, only admins and doctors hold presence and nurses get nothing new.

product_rulings.question: ADT-S8. May a non-clinical clerk change a patient's treating department? That changes who can read the chart; frontdesk_routes.py:140-161 calls it 'not a bedside decision'.
product_rulings.options: (a) Never; clinicians only. (b) Only to carry out a transfer a doctor has already ordered, with the ordering doctor named. (c) Freely within the clerk's department.
product_rulings.recommendation: (b). Until ruled, the clerk holds ADT_BED only (moves that keep the treating department).

product_rulings.question: ADT-S9. When a registered patient is readmitted, what carries over from the previous stay: the last vitals and risk row (which would show as 'latest' on the board, NEWS2 and Sage until a new set is charted), the Sage room memory, and the case room history?
product_rulings.options: (a) Previous-stay vitals shown only with their date and a 'previous stay' label, never as current latest; Sage memory archived and restarted; case room reused with a dividing system line. (b) Everything carries as today's data. (c) Nothing visible from the previous stay.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). The readmit entry point stays closed until this is ruled.

product_rulings.question: F104 (open). Should the server refuse a ward or bed the hospital has not configured?
product_rulings.options: Refuse once setup is done (ORB_ADT_STRICT_LOCATIONS), or warn only.
product_rulings.recommendation: Warn (keep typed text unlinked) until the bed manager marks setup complete, then turn strict on per site.

product_rulings.question: ADT-P2. Does the Ward Record profile turn ORB_ADT on for its clerk pickers, moves and 'left the ward' (sales plan item 184)?
product_rulings.options: (a) Yes, with census, reservations, housekeeping and billing parts off. (b) Build a separate lighter clerk flow.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a): one ADT writer and no second free-text lane to retire. Re-cost the Ward Record admission work at about 54.5 engineer-days plus OPD create-or-find, not 11 to 17.5, and say plainly that clerk admission and 'left the ward' cannot ship until S5 and S3 are ruled, and the returning patient until S9.

product_rulings.question: ADT-P3. How far back may admission, transfer and departure times be entered, and by whom?
product_rulings.options: A window in hours; older entries by an admin with a reason.
product_rulings.recommendation: 72 h for ADT writers; older needs an admin and a reason; show both event time and recorded time.

product_rulings.question: ADT-P4. What is the occupancy denominator and census method?
product_rulings.options: Licensed vs available beds; midnight census vs hour-based inpatient days.
product_rulings.recommendation: Report both; the NABH indicator uses available beds and midnight census and states the method.

product_rulings.question: ADT-P5. Should the capacity screens take bed counts from the master per ward once that ward's register is complete?
product_rulings.options: Yes per ward; or keep ORB_WARD_BEDS everywhere.
product_rulings.recommendation: Yes per ward, labelled 'from bed register'; ORB_WARD_BEDS stays the fallback.

product_rulings.question: ADT-P6. On leave: is the bed held, is room rent charged, and how long before a leave becomes a discharge?
product_rulings.options: Held or released; charged or not; maximum length.
product_rulings.recommendation: Held; rent per site setting (default charged); leave over 48 h prompts the doctor to discharge.

product_rulings.question: ADT-P8. On death, what is closed automatically: portal login, discharge link, diet orders, pending pharmacy orders, the Relay case room?
product_rulings.options: Any subset, in the death transaction or as follow-up tasks.
product_rulings.recommendation: Deactivate the portal login (restored only by a reopen), no discharge link, stop diet orders, Relay room read-only; pending pharmacy orders when the single medication-order store lands. Nothing deleted. Until ruled, adt-8a issues no link and leaves the login as today.

product_rulings.question: ADT-P9. Default bed reservation expiry?
product_rulings.options: Minutes per purpose.
product_rulings.recommendation: 120 min for ER and transfer, 24 h for elective and post-op, site-configurable.

risks: Migration collisions: eight new migrations (provisional 48 to 55) while about ten sessions add migrations. Claim each number at build time and run test_migrations.

Release gate: switching ORB_ADT on at a site where Sage runs before adt-6c lets the Relay transfer lane change departments outside the ledger, so census misses transfers and patients silently become boarders. The gate is written next to ORB_ADT in config.

The Relay lane has a flag-OFF defect today: its department list is every user's department, including patient portal logins whose users.department holds a WARD label (admission_service.py:259-262), so a ward label could be written into admissions.department and drop the patient off every board. adt-6c fixes it only with the flag on; it deserves its own fix for all sites (recommend a separate task once the Relay session lands).

Text mirrors: about 34 server files read patients.ward/bed and admissions.ward/bed. Any ADT write that skips locate_admission_on desyncs boards, Sage, I-PASS, the downtime pack and housekeeping. Mitigation: single writer, rename immutability, housekeeping register refusal for beds, parity test.

The partial unique index is the first constraint that can refuse an admission write; callers must catch db_backend.DBIntegrityError and answer 409 with words. bed_id is NULL with the flag off, so the index never fires; tests pin it.
Boarders stay invisible to host-ward nurses until S6. The acknowledgement makes it explicit and audited, but the board will make the gap visible to staff, and a full home ward makes boarding routine.
Cleaning state is a pull. The board's ledger rule keeps a vacated bed out of 'available' without a sync, but housekeeping's own screen can lag until the sync runs.

Adoption on a live site: active admissions have no bed_id and some share a typed bed. Reconciliation must finish by hand before register-complete; until then the ward's census reports insufficient data, which will look like a missing feature.

The opt-in flag departs from the 2026-08-11 'all modules default on' ruling pinned in test_money and the shell; the shell cache must keep adt false on any failed probe or a Beds tab flashes whose routes 404.

Sizing: the honest figure is about 78.5 engineer-days for the epic, 41.5 for the core, and about 54.5 for the Ward Record minimum plus OPD create-or-find, against 11 to 17.5 assumed in the sales plan. This affects the Ward Record timeline.

Death and LAMA are medico-legal records. Server read-back, the reopen-by-correction flow and void-not-delete reduce the wrong-patient harm; a stay with a discharge summary still cannot be reopened, only followed by a new admission.

The escalation ladder tick has no patient-status filter (escalation_service.py:887-893), so chains keep escalating after any end of stay, including death. That is R009 territory (held); this design lists open chains at end of stay and closes none. R009's answer should be read as covering every end type.
The vitals simulator writes vitals for every admitted patient; until adt-11 a patient on leave can get simulated readings (under honesty labels).

issues.issue: Board precedence hides a patient. out_of_service ranks above occupied, so an occupied bed that housekeeping marks out of service shows as 'out of service' with no occupant. occupied to out_of_service is a legal housekeeping transition, and nurses hold the write gate (vitals.write). adt-3's test pins this behaviour ('out_of_service beats everything except retired').

Change the adt-3 precedence test to pin that. locate_admission_on should refuse or warn on an out_of_service or retired bed.

issues.issue: A bed that has just been vacated can show as available. needs_cleaning is derived only when housekeeping says 'occupied' and nobody occupies the bed. If housekeeping never recorded the bed as occupied, it stays vacant_ready, and the departure leaves it reading 'available'. That happens for every move before adt-7 lands, when the best-effort sync fails or lags, and for an admit plus move-out between two sync runs. adt-5 (the BedPicker) depends on adt-3 but not adt-7, so the admit picker would offer uncleaned beds as clean. This is an infection-control hole on the bed after an isolation patient.
issues.evidence: Design section 4 rule 5. adt-5 depends_on [adt-2, adt-3, adt-4], not adt-7. housekeeping_service.py:1078-1126: the sweep is a pull that runs on board load.
issues.fix: Also derive needs_cleaning from the ledger: if the bed's latest vacating movement (from_bed_id) has a moved_at newer than the unit's state_since for vacant_ready, the bed needs cleaning, whatever housekeeping says. Pin it with a test that has no sync. Make adt-5 depend on this rule rather than on adt-7.

issues.issue: An ordering defect makes adt-2 unshippable as written. adt-2 builds the reconciliation link and record_movement_on 'writing to today's ledger shape'. If the link writes a 'transfer' row instead, it is a fake transfer that billing's _admission_moves reads, because it does not filter by type until adt-4. patient_movements is also created lazily, so it may not exist yet at adt-2.
issues.evidence: frontdesk_service.py:203-205 CHECK (movement_type IN ('transfer','admission','discharge')); billing_service.py:1046-1050 reads every row for the admission with no type filter; adt-4 depends_on adt-2

issues.issue: The housekeeping register stays a second bed writer. It can also relabel a master bed that has a patient in it. POST /api/housekeeping/units, open to anyone with vitals.write, takes the non-create_only path, which rewrites ward and bed_label of an existing unit_code. When ORB_ADT is on, that desyncs housekeeping_units.ward from wards.code and admissions and patients text from the bed. register_unit also passes the ward through _canonical_ward, which can store a patient's typed spelling ('gm-1') instead of wards.code, which breaks 'ward text column kept equal to wards.code'.
issues.evidence: housekeeping_routes.py:323-343; housekeeping_service.py:466-488 (UPDATE ... SET ward = ?, bed_label = COALESCE(?, bed_label)); housekeeping_service.py:349-371 _canonical_ward matches against patients.ward first

issues.issue: Renaming a ward code or a bed label in the master has no defined effect on the text mirrors. PATCH /master/wards and update_bed can change the labels that 50+ files read from admissions.ward/bed and patients.ward/bed. Nurses, the eMAR round and Sage identify patients by those labels. A silent relabel of an occupied bed is a wrong-patient risk.
issues.evidence: Design section 6: POST/PATCH /master/wards, /master/beds; update_bed has no stated guard. locate_admission_on is the only mirror writer.
issues.fix: Make wards.code and a bed label immutable once any admission references them (retire and recreate instead), or refuse a rename while the bed is occupied or reserved. If renames must be allowed, cascade them through locate_admission_on with a 'location_linked' or 'correction' movement and an audit row, and test mirror parity after the rename.

issues.issue: Swaps and corrections are toggles, and their scope checks are one-sided. Scope is checked 'on the sending side' only, so a swap lets a clerk or doctor move another department's patient. No idempotency key or expected-state check is specified, so a double-submitted or retried swap silently swaps the patients back. The board then puts the wrong patient in the wrong bed, which is a wrong-patient hazard.
issues.evidence: Design section 6: 'scope checked on the sending side'. patient_movements already has idx_movements_idempotency (frontdesk_service.py:236), but the ADT routes do not mention idempotency.
issues.fix: Require both admissions in a swap to be in scope (404 otherwise). Require an Idempotency-Key on every ADT write. Make swap, change, transfer and correct carry the expected current bed_id(s) and refuse with 409 when the state has moved on.

issues.issue: Lanes that send only text behave inconsistently with ORB_ADT on and strict mode off. List unlinked typed beds separately from awaiting-bed, and have assign refuse when bed text is present unless the request is an explicit correction. Make bed Optional only when ORB_ADT is on, and keep the flag-off 422 contract.

issues.issue: The ledger has no defined start, so census and NABH results before cutover are wrong. Midnight census, ALOS and the return-to-ICU count read the movement ledger. Undercounting ICU returns makes the hospital look better, which breaks nabh_service's stated rule that a pack may only be wrong in the worse direction.

Refuse, or label 'insufficient data', for any census day or indicator window before it. Fall back to discharge_summaries for ends before the flag. Add a test for a window that straddles cutover. Re-size adt-13 to about 5 to 6 days.

Nothing reopens a stay that was wrongly ended: status, the portal login, the disposition row, cancelled bundles. The read-back confirmation is UI-only, so an API client can record a death with no check.

issues.issue: The design builds boarder placement as a first-class workflow ahead of S6. The board and BedPicker make it routine to put a patient on another department's ward, where the host-ward nurses physically caring for the patient cannot open the chart. That is the orphaning failure frontdesk_service calls 'the worst outcome this file can produce', now offered as a feature.

It is audited as clinical_access and surfaced to the treating team (for example a Relay system line). Or refuse it while ORB_ADT_STRICT_LOCATIONS is on. Do not decide S6.

issues.issue: Bulk bed registration is not atomic and its audit is not transactional. register_unit opens its own db_session per call, so register_beds of 24 beds is 24 transactions: a 409 halfway leaves a partial ward. The bed_master_events row and the audit cannot share the same transaction.

issues.issue: The cover check could deadlock if it moves inside the immediate transaction. locate_admission_on(db) 'checks the ward's cover', but list_covering_departments opens its own db_session and calls ensure_frontdesk_schema, which can run DDL. On the unpooled path that second connection waits on the outer write lock for the full busy_timeout. transfer_patient deliberately resolves cover before BEGIN IMMEDIATE.
issues.evidence: frontdesk_service.py:332-354 and :1113-1119 (resolved before db_session(immediate=True)); database.py:1124-1158 (immediate must be outermost; unpooled nested sessions contend)

issues.issue: Dual audit and dual turnaround-task risks when lanes delegate. With the flag on, frontdesk delegates to adt_service, which audits inside the transaction, but the route's own post-commit clinical_access audit would still fire. A routine discharge creates a task keyed by summary id from sync_discharge_turnarounds and potentially another from sync_adt_movements keyed by movement.

issues.issue: Automatic NABH dispositions can double-count. The unique key is (patient_id, occurred_at), so an admin-keyed disposition for the same stay with a different timestamp plus the automatic one gives two rows, and mortality is double-counted.

issues.fix: Before inserting, look up an existing disposition for the same admission_id (or the same patient within the stay window) and update it, or refuse and flag it for reconciliation. Add a test.

issues.issue: admitted_at gets two sources. A back-timed admission sets admitted_at, but bed-day billing, forecast 'admissions today' and nabh read created_at or admission_date, so the bill and the census disagree on when the stay started.

issues.issue: Migration and DDL hazards are understated. (1) housekeeping_units columns are added only in M-a, while HOUSEKEEPING_TABLES stays shared with the lazy ensure_housekeeping_schema, which recreates the drift that sharing was meant to prevent. (2) The patient_movements rebuild must copy rowid, because readers break ties on rowid. (3) 'Flag off is byte-identical' overstates it: every migration runs unconditionally on every encrypted DB, and SELECT * readers return the new NULL columns. (4) The new CHECK on movement_type means a future widening needs another rebuild, while admissions uses triggers to avoid exactly that.
issues.evidence: housekeeping_service.py:244-265 and migrations.py:2994; frontdesk_service.py:1240-1246 and billing_service.py:1048 (rowid tiebreaks)
issues.fix: Fold the new columns into the lazy path, or guard the lazy path with ALTER. Copy rowid explicitly in M-c. Restate the flag-off guarantee as 'no behaviour change; schema changes always apply'. Consider replacing the CHECK with a vocabulary trigger, like admissions.

Checked against the code on 3 Oct 2026. The latest migration is 47 (vitals_carried_from, server/migrations.py:5417; registry at :5446), so new migrations start at 48. Claim the number when you build, because about ten sessions add migrations.

TABLES

- admissions: department, ward and bed are free text. status CHECK is ('active','discharged','transferred') (database.py:69-89). admissions.discharged_at exists, but only imported encounters set it (migrations.py:1432, m15). No table REFERENCES admissions. patients is the FK parent of about 35 references.

1. PRINCIPLES
- One source per fact.
  - Occupancy is derived from the admission (admissions.bed_id on an active admission), the same way scope is derived live from admissions.department.
  - Cleaning state stays with housekeeping.
  - patient_movements is the history.
  - The text mirrors (patients.ward/bed, admissions.ward/bed) are still written, because about 34 server files read them. They are written from master labels by ONE writer, adt_service.locate_admission_on.
- No new value in patients.status or admissions.status.
  - 22 readers filter on 'admitted'/'active', and widening the CHECK would mean rebuilding patients, which is an FK parent.
  - On leave and absconded live in admissions.presence_status.
  - Every end of stay is status 'discharged' plus admissions.discharge_type.
- Flag off means byte-identical.
  - Every new column stays NULL and every /api/adt route returns 404.
  - Existing suites pass unchanged, and snapshot tests pin the rows written by admit, transfer and discharge with the flag off.
- Additive migrations only:
  - ADD COLUMN;
  - new tables with NO foreign keys (the m20/m22 rule);
  - partial and expression indexes;
  - one statement per execute, never executescript;
  - IF NOT EXISTS plus PRAGMA table_info guards.
  - The only rebuild is patient_movements, which has no FK children and is safe inside the runner's transaction.
  - patients and admissions are never rebuilt. users is rebuilt only through _rebuild_users_role_check.
- Every ADT write:
  - runs in db_session(immediate=True);
  - writes its audit inside the same transaction (log_audit_event(db=...)), so an audit that cannot be written rolls the move back;
  - catches db_backend.DBIntegrityError, never sqlite3.IntegrityError;
  - stamps times with services.clinical_time.utc_iso_now()/to_utc_iso();
  - passes target_id as a string (the int target_id chain break).

2. FEATURE FLAGS (server/config.py)

3. DATA MODEL

M-a (adt-1), the bed master:
- facilities(code PK, name, is_active, created_at, updated_at).
  - Bed setup creates the first row from the site name. The migration seeds nothing.
  - The multi-site epic extends this table.
- wards(id PK 'WRD-...', facility_code NOT NULL DEFAULT 'MAIN', code NOT NULL, name, department NOT NULL, ward_type CHECK(general,icu,hdu,nicu,picu,maternity,daycare,emergency,isolation,other), default_bed_class, register_complete INT DEFAULT 0, register_complete_at, register_complete_by, is_active, created_by, created_at, updated_at).
  - code is the label written to admissions.ward, for example GM-1.
  - department is the canonical spelling of a covering department.
  - UNIQUE INDEX on (facility_code, LOWER(TRIM(code))), so 'gm-1' can never become a phantom ward.
- ward_rooms(id PK, ward_id NOT NULL, code, name, room_type CHECK(bay,private,semi_private,isolation,icu_cubicle,other), is_isolation INT, gender_policy CHECK(any,male,female) DEFAULT 'any' (warn only), is_active, timestamps).
  - UNIQUE on (ward_id, LOWER(TRIM(code))).
- bed_classes(code PK, name, bed_day_service_code, is_critical_care INT, counts_in_census INT DEFAULT 1, sort_order, is_active, timestamps).
  - No seed: a class nobody configured is not a class.
- housekeeping_units ADD COLUMN ward_id, room_id, bed_class, counts_in_census INT (NULL means inherit from the class), is_temporary INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 (an extra or overflow bed), sort_key, retired_at.
  - INDEX on (ward_id, is_active, sort_key).
  - A unit with unit_type 'bed' IS the physical bed. 'room', 'bay' and 'theatre' units stay cleaning objects only.
  - The ward text column is kept equal to wards.code.
- bed_master_events(id, entity_type CHECK(facility,ward,room,bed,bed_class), entity_id, action, detail_json, reason, actor_user_id, occurred_at).
  - Append-only through no-update and no-delete triggers.
  - It holds no patient data, so it stays out of the W165 erasure problem.

M-b (adt-2), where the admission is:
- admissions ADD COLUMN:
  - ward_id, bed_id;
  - bed_shared_reason;
  - admitted_at: canonical UTC; readers use COALESCE(admitted_at, created_at);
  - presence_status: NULL means on the ward, otherwise on_leave or absconded; plus presence_since;
  - discharge_type: NULL, or the NABH vocabulary routine, referred_out, transferred_out, dama, lama, absconded, death;
  - discharged_by.
- discharged_at already exists (m15). It is now also set for Orb-native ends when ORB_ADT is on.
- The vocabularies are enforced by BEFORE INSERT and BEFORE UPDATE OF presence_status, discharge_type triggers (RAISE ABORT), not by a CHECK.
  - Widening a vocabulary is then DROP/CREATE TRIGGER, not a rebuild of a hot clinical table.
  - Ordinary admission updates do not fire them.
  - A note beside _atomic_table_rebuild says any future admissions rebuild must carry these triggers.
- The bed lock: UNIQUE INDEX idx_admissions_active_bed ON admissions(bed_id) WHERE status='active' AND bed_id IS NOT NULL AND bed_shared_reason IS NULL.
  - The database refuses an accidental double booking, such as two clerks racing for one bed.
  - A deliberate shared bed must carry a reason (ruling S1 decides whether this path survives).
  - The index is created safely because every existing bed_id is NULL.
- INDEX on (ward_id, status).

M-c (adt-4), the ledger:
- patient_movements moves into a numbered migration that handles three cases: the table is absent (create it), it has the old shape (rebuild inside the transaction and recreate its 3 indexes), or it already has the new shape (do nothing).
- frontdesk_service then imports its DDL from migrations, as housekeeping does.
- New columns: from_ward_id, from_bed_id, to_ward_id, to_bed_id, end_type, discharge_summary_id, corrects_movement_id, recorded_at.
- movement_type is widened to: admission, bed_assigned, transfer, bed_change, bed_swap, leave_start, leave_end, absconded, absconded_return, discharge, location_linked, correction.
- moved_at is when it happened (it can be back-timed). recorded_at is the server clock.
- Rows are never updated. A correction is a new row that points at the old one.
- New indexes on (to_bed_id, moved_at), (from_bed_id, moved_at) and (movement_type, moved_at).

Further migrations:
- M-d (adt-7): housekeeping_movement_links(movement_id PK, unit_id, effect CHECK(occupied,occupied_unclean,vacated,task_raised,skipped), task_id, applied_at). It is the database idempotency guard for the pull sync.

4. BED STATUS ON THE BOARD
Derived, in this order of precedence:
1. retired
2. out_of_service (housekeeping)
3. occupied, occupied_on_leave or occupied_absconded (an active admission holds the bed)
4. reserved
5. needs_cleaning: the unit is vacant_dirty, or housekeeping says 'occupied' while nobody occupies it. That means the patient left and no clean is recorded, and it is never shown as available.
6. cleaning
7. available (vacant_ready)

Each tile carries minutes in state, isolation and temporary markers, and the bed class. For an occupant inside the caller's scope it also shows name, MRN and treating department, plus 'Boarder from <dept>' when that department differs from the ward's.

product_rulings.question: ADT-S1. When the chosen bed already holds an admitted patient, what happens? Today the admission is warned, never blocked (admission_service.py:120 says this is the founder's call). The bed label is how nurses, the eMAR round and Sage find a patient.
product_rulings.options: (a) Block, and offer 'add an extra bed' that creates a temporary bed with its own label (GM-1/12A). (b) Allow a deliberate shared bed with a typed reason, recorded; accidental double booking is refused by the database either way. (c) Keep today's warning only.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). Every patient keeps a unique bed label, and an extra bed is counted honestly as temporary. Until ruled, the build ships (b), which is today's warning made explicit.

product_rulings.question: ADT-S2. May a patient be admitted or transferred into a bed that housekeeping has not recorded as clean, including a bed awaiting a terminal clean after an isolation patient?
product_rulings.options: (a) Allow with a reason, recorded as 'occupied without completed clean' (today's housekeeping design). (b) Warn only. (c) Block beds awaiting a terminal clean unless a named person authorises it; allow standard-clean beds with a reason.
product_rulings.recommendation: (c). It keeps the 3 a.m. reality for ordinary beds and stops the infection-control harm. Until ruled, the build warns and records.

product_rulings.question: ADT-S3. Who may end an admission, by type: routine departure after a doctor's discharge, LAMA, DAMA, absconded closure, death? Also, may the Ward Record clerk mark 'left the ward' with no discharge summary?
product_rulings.options: Per type: doctor only; doctor or nurse; clerk or bed manager; time windows for absconded closure.
product_rulings.recommendation: Death, LAMA and DAMA stay doctor-only (discharge.generate, ward-scoped, read-back confirmation), as today. A nurse or clerk records the physical departure only after a doctor's discharge exists. The bed manager closes an absconded stay after 24 h (site setting), with police intimation noted for MLC cases. In the Ward Record profile the clerk may record 'left the ward' with the time.

product_rulings.question: ADT-S4. While a patient is on leave or absconded, do they stay on clinical boards? Do obs-due timers, medication-due lists, escalation ladders, sepsis auto-start and the vitals simulator keep running?
product_rulings.options: (a) Stay on boards with a 'Not on ward' chip; obs and med due paused with the reason shown; escalation paused, not closed; resumes on return. (b) Remove from boards until return. (c) No change.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). Absconded patients with an open escalation also notify the treating doctor in Relay. Removing them recreates the orphaning failure.

product_rulings.question: ADT-S5. May a non-clinical ward clerk create an admission? What does the chart show for allergies and other clinical fields until a clinician completes them? Orb cannot tell NKDA from 'never asked' today (allergy_interlock.py:364).
product_rulings.options: (a) Yes: a registration-level admission whose clinical fields read 'Not yet assessed', never NKDA; the interlock treats it as unknown; the board flags 'admission assessment due'. (b) Clerks may not admit; only doctors.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). It is required for the Ward Record and for front-office admission. 'Not yet assessed' must never print as NKDA.

product_rulings.question: ADT-S6. A boarder is a patient lying on another department's ward. Today scope follows the treating department only, so the host ward's nurses cannot open the chart of a patient in their own beds. Whose board are they on?
product_rulings.options: (a) Both: host-ward nurses get shift-board and nursing access, and the treating team keeps medical ownership. (b) Treating department only (today). (c) The ward's department only.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). It is built as one change to permissions.PATIENT_DEPARTMENT_SQL and its sage_service twin, under the parity test. Until ruled, ADT records and labels boarders and scope is unchanged.

product_rulings.question: F104 (open). Should the server refuse a ward or bed the hospital has not configured?
product_rulings.options: Refuse once setup is done (ORB_ADT_STRICT_LOCATIONS), or warn only.
product_rulings.recommendation: As F104 recommends: warn until the bed manager marks setup complete, then turn strict on per site.

product_rulings.question: ADT-P2. Does the Ward Record profile turn ORB_ADT on for its clerk pickers, moves and 'left the ward' (sales plan item 184)?
product_rulings.options: (a) Yes, with census, reservations and billing parts left off. (b) Build a separate lighter clerk flow.
product_rulings.recommendation: (a). One ADT writer, and no second free-text lane to retire later. Re-cost the Ward Record admission work at about 32 engineer-days, not 11 to 17.5.

product_rulings.question: ADT-P3. How far back may admission, transfer and departure times be entered, and by whom?
product_rulings.options: A window in hours; older entries by an admin with a reason.
product_rulings.recommendation: 72 h for ADT writers, so a clerk can key the morning after a holiday. Older entries need an admin and a reason. Show both the event time and the recorded time.

product_rulings.question: ADT-P4. What is the occupancy denominator and the census method?
product_rulings.options: Licensed beds vs available beds (census beds minus out-of-service time); midnight census vs hour-based inpatient days.
product_rulings.recommendation: Report both. The NABH indicator uses available beds and midnight census, and states the method.

product_rulings.question: ADT-P5. Should the capacity screens (Forecast, Command Center, Vigil occupancy tile, housekeeping readiness) take bed counts from the master per ward once that ward's register is marked complete?
product_rulings.options: Yes per ward; or keep ORB_WARD_BEDS everywhere.
product_rulings.recommendation: Yes per ward, labelled 'from bed register'. ORB_WARD_BEDS stays the fallback.

product_rulings.question: ADT-P6. On leave: is the bed held, is room rent charged, and how long before a leave becomes a discharge?
product_rulings.options: Bed held or released; charged or not; maximum leave length.
product_rulings.recommendation: The bed is held. Room rent follows a site setting (default charged). Leave over 48 h prompts the doctor to discharge.

product_rulings.question: ADT-P7. Do nurses get the Beds tab (read-only board scoped to their ward, plus leave and absconded recording)? That puts 'adt' in CLINICAL_MODULE_IDS.

product_rulings.question: ADT-P8. On death, what is closed automatically: portal login, discharge link, diet orders, pending pharmacy orders, the Relay case room?
product_rulings.options: Any subset, in the death transaction or as follow-up tasks.

product_rulings.question: ADT-P9. What is the default expiry for a bed reservation?
product_rulings.options: Minutes, per purpose.
product_rulings.recommendation: 120 min for ER and transfer, 24 h for elective and post-op. Site-configurable.

Text mirrors. About 34 server files read patients.ward/bed and admissions.ward/bed. Any new ADT writer that skips locate_admission_on desyncs the boards, Sage, I-PASS, the downtime pack and housekeeping. Mitigation: a single writer plus a parity test (bed_id label equals both mirrors for every linked active admission).

The partial unique index is the first constraint that can refuse an admission write. sqlcipher raises its own IntegrityError, so callers must catch db_backend.DBIntegrityError and turn it into a 409 with words. With the flag off, bed_id is NULL and the index never fires; tests must pin that.
Scope moves with transfers (strict handover). Boarders stay invisible to the host ward's nurses until S6 is ruled. That is today's behaviour, but the bed board will make it visible to staff.

Housekeeping is a pull. Cleaning state can lag behind occupancy for a short time. The board rule 'housekeeping says occupied, nobody occupies' must read as needs cleaning, never available. A test pins it.

Adoption on a live site. Existing active admissions have no bed_id and some share a free-text bed. Reconciliation must be finished by hand before strict mode, and the dev DB seeds doubled labels for some fixtures.

Sizing. The coverage map's '1.5 to 2 weeks' for the bed master and board and the sales plan's 11 to 17.5 days for the Ward Record clerk screens leave out reconciliation, the lock, in-transaction audit, the housekeeping link and scope. Death and LAMA are medico-legal records. Recording one against the wrong patient is severe. A read-back confirmation (name, MRN, bed) and a correction-by-new-row flow are required; nothing may be deletable.
The vitals simulator (bot_service) writes vitals for every admitted patient. Until adt-11 lands, a patient on leave can get simulated readings, under honesty labels.

R009 surface. New end-of-stay doors (absconded closure, the clerk's departure) could bypass whatever R009 decides unless every door calls discharge_preconditions. A test must assert that all end_stay callers go through it.
Audit semantics change. Adding 'patient_movement' to the fail-closed set means an audit-table failure now blocks bed moves. That is intended, but it widens the fail-closed blast radius at 3 a.m.

Readers keyed on discharge_summaries. Housekeeping sweep, NABH inpatient days and the /discharged list treat a summary as proof of discharge. Summary-less ends (death, LAMA, the Ward Record departure) must be taught to every reader, or they look like stays that never ended.
